title: Cross-org priority sync — initiative check-in (Oct 27 2027)
content:
Purpose:
Quick cross-org check-in during the engineering all-hands focused on the three-quarter initiatives: autoscaling refinements, canary rollout hygiene, and KV/prefix cache improvements for short-tail latency workloads. This doc captures highlights, decisions, open questions, and next steps.

Attendees (note: not exhaustive):
- Daniel Kim (owner) — platform lead
- Lina Zhao — infra (autoscaling)
- Rafael Gomez — serving-runtime lead
- Priya Menon — product (hosted API)
- Maya Thompson — SRE
- ~40 engineers across serving-runtime, platform, dedicated, private

Highlights from the update:
- Autoscaling alpha policy rollout (region us-west-2) completed for gen-2 dedicated pools. Early results: 7% improvement in sustained throughput during weekday peak; 12% reduction in cold-start tail latency for bursty workloads. (see INF-2312)
- Canary deployment hygiene checklist adopted company-wide: automatic traffic-shift windows, rollback latency thresholds, and mandatory perf/eval gating for model-promote PRs.
- KV/prefix cache experiment (small shards) shows 9–13% reduction in per-token cost for 2048-seq chat traces after enabling selective prefix caching for system prompts. Still WIP — more traffic shapes needed.

Data & metrics called out:
- Autoscale: scale-up time median: 18s -> 12s post-tuning; maximum observed cold-start tail still ~2.4s for new node attach during extreme bursts (weekend stress).
- Canary traffic: mean error delta across canaries <0.02 for top 10 customers; two canaries flagged for higher mismatch (CSR-602 and CSR-607).
- Cost: projected monthly savings if autoscale tuning goes to prod across all pools: ~$42k. (back-of-envelope; finance to confirm)

What shipped since last all-hands:
- Migration of the autoscaler control plane to the new state-store with incremental reconciles (reduces noisy churn in pools).
- Serving-runtime now exposes a lightweight adhoc tracing span for kv-cache hits; requires a small agent update in Dedicated.
- Product published the canary playbook and example rollout YAML in the console docs (internal link in artifacts).

Open issues / risks called out:
- Canaries passing perf but diverging on quality for a subset of prompts (edge-case few-shot formatting). Need dedicated eval harness run labeled "canary-formatting-v2".
- Region capacity mismatch: apac pooled demand is growing faster than forecast; risk for Private customers who pin to APAC regions. Ops requested two-week runway to add capacity.
- Observability gap: token-level cost traces are not yet correlated with model-variant metadata in some legacy dashboards. This blocks fine-grained cost attribution for Reserved contracts.

Decisions made during the sync:
- Short-term: expand autoscaler config rollout to 3 more dedicated pools (EU central, APAC-east, US-east-2) on Nov 3 gated by a smoke test. Owner: Lina.
- Medium-term: require a mandatory eval set run for any canary >10% traffic shift or involving model architecture changes. Owner: Rafael + product.
- Immediate: spin up a focused "KV cache traceathon" (2-day hack) to build representative traffic shapes and synthetic prefixes. Owner: Maya.

Action items (owner — due):
- Lina — schedule pool rollout and post-rollout report (Nov 10).
- Rafael — add canary-eval gating to the promotion pipeline; draft PR and RFC (Nov 2).
- Priya — coordinate with CS to run targeted quality checks for CSR-602/607 and surface prompt variants (Oct 30).
- Maya — run the KV cache traceathon and publish traffic shapes + tickets for follow-ups (Nov 4).
- Daniel — follow up with finance for confirmed savings estimate and update the exec one-pager (Nov 8).

Notes to self / informal fragments captured during Q&A:
- "We still see a few tenants where quantized model variants return slight punctuation shifts — looks like tokenization corner cases."
- "Would love a small sample set of real customer prompts for the eval harness — CS said they can provide two customer buckets."
- TODO: add a short checklist to the canary playbook: 'confirm KV cache warmup threshold' and 'confirm tokenization parity test'.
- Action: check whether the state-store reconcile interval can be pushed to 200ms without causing flaps (current is 500ms).

Cross-team help requested:
- Solutions engineering: help collect representative customer prompt bins for quality evaluation (Priya to intro).
- Observability: add model-variant tag to token-cost traces in the short term (Maya/Tony pair).
- Eng Payroll/People Ops: support hiring plan for two infra SWE ICs focusing on autoscaling (hiring need flagged).

FAQ / common questions from attendees:
Q: Will canaries continue to use traffic split by customer?
A: Yes — we reserve a small set of deterministic customers for safety and random traffic slices for scale validation. Expanded gating will require both perf and quality checks.

Q: Is Dedicated capacity going to get more aggressive burst capacity?
A: We will pilot increased burst headroom in two pools; pricing/comms TBD. Product and finance to collaborate.

Next follow-up forum:
- Cross-org initiative deep-dive (1 hour): Nov 11 10:00–11:00 PT — focus on KV cache results and canary gating. Prep: Rafael to circulate perf dashboards 48h prior.

Attachments / artifacts to review before the deep-dive:
- INF-2312 autoscaler tuning notes (Linear)
- Confluence: kv-cache-optimizations (internal)
- Canary playbook (Console docs link)

Closing thoughts (from leadership):
- Good momentum on the infra side — incremental wins on latency/cost. Keep shipping small, measurable improvements and surface any customer-impacting anomalies immediately.
- Emphasis on cross-team test harnesses and shared traffic shapes — these are the glue that will let us scale changes with confidence.

Raw meeting transcript snippets (copied rough):
- "We need more synthetic shells that mimic ephemeral chat sessions — not just long-tail batch traces." — Rafael
- "If Finance can sign off on the $42k, that buys another HC for infra next quarter." — Daniel

End notes / housekeeping:
- This doc is a working capture from the all-hands update — please add inline comments or follow-ups.
- If you want to join the KV traceathon or volunteer to review canary evals, ping @Maya or add yourself to the tracker: INF-2380.

-- DK
